candidates.exact_span: Seven representative samples of the sewage sludge that is disposed shall be collected for one monitoring episode at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of how many samples constitute compliance, what counts as one monitoring episode, and whether use versus disposal triggers the obligation would change which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable and whether missing results reflect required monitoring or a documented no-data state.

candidates.exact_span: The geometric mean of the density of fecal coliform in the samples collected shall be less than either 2,000,000 Most Probable Number per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) or 2,000,000 Colony Forming Units per gram of total solids (dry weight basis).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of geometric-mean calculation method, dry-weight basis, and whether MPN or CFU is the operative unit would change the enforceable numeric limit applied to reported measurements and which monitoring parameter is required for comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 2 - Sewage sludge shall be treated in one of the Processes to significantly Reduce Pathogens described in 503 Appendix B.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If a facility is treated as complying through this process-based alternative rather than the fecal-coliform numeric limit, the applicable enforceable standard and expected monitoring evidence shift from numeric comparison to process compliance, changing limit applicability and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 3 - Sewage sludge shall be treated in a process that is equivalent to a PSRP, if individually approved by the Pathogen Equivalency Committee representing the EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether individual Pathogen Equivalency Committee approval is established determines whether this alternative applies instead of numeric fecal-coliform limits, affecting which compliance standard is operative and whether absent approval evidence leaves obligations unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 4 - Sewage sludge placed on an active surface disposal site is covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of active surface disposal site, what qualifies as soil or other material, and what constitutes each operating day affects whether this pathogen-reduction alternative is satisfied and what operational monitoring or documentation is required versus treated as not applicable.

candidates.exact_span: All sewage sludge that is disposed of in a surface disposal site shall be treated by one of the following alternatives 1 through 11 for Vector Attraction Reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is characterized as disposed at a surface disposal site and which vector-attraction alternative is selected determines the set of enforceable requirements and monitoring obligations that apply, and whether absent evidence reflects non-applicability or unresolved compliance.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 1 - The mass of volatile solids in the sewage sludge shall be reduced by a minimum of 38%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretations of how volatile-solids reduction is measured and over what treatment interval would change whether the 38% threshold is the applicable numeric limit and whether corresponding monitoring is required.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 2 - If Alternative 1 cannot be met for an anaerobically digested sludge, demonstration can be made by digesting a portion of the previously digested sludge anaerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 40 additional days at a temperature between 30 and 37 degrees Celsius. Volatile solids must be reduced by less than 17% to demonstrate compliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Alternative 1 is considered unmet, whether bench-scale conditions are satisfied, and how the less-than-17% volatile-solids-reduction criterion is evaluated would change the applicable compliance test, required supplemental monitoring, and classification of missing demonstration data.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 3 - If Alternative 1 cannot be met for an aerobically digested sludge, demonstration can be made by digesting a portion of the previously digested sludge with a percent solid of two percent or less aerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 30 additional days at 20 degrees Celsius. Volatile solids must be reduced by less than 15% to demonstrate compliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of aerobic-sludge eligibility, the two-percent-solids precondition, bench-test protocol, and the less-than-15% pass/fail threshold would change which numeric criterion applies and whether monitoring or demonstration evidence is required versus unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 4 - The specific oxygen uptake rate (SOUR) for sewage sludge treated in an aerobic process shall be equal to or less than 1.5 milligrams of oxygen per hour per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) at a temperature of 20 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of SOUR measurement conditions, dry-weight basis, and the 20 degrees Celsius requirement would change the enforceable numeric limit used for comparison and whether SOUR monitoring is an applicable obligation.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 5 - Sewage sludge shall be treated in an aerobic process for 14 days or longer. During that time, the temperature of the sewage sludge shall be higher than 40 degrees Celsius and the average temperature of the sewage sludge shall be higher than 45 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How treatment duration, instantaneous versus average temperature, and the measurement window are interpreted would change whether temperature-based compliance is established and what monitoring evidence is expected for periods without reported temperature data.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 6 - The pH of sewage sludge shall be raised to 12 or higher by alkali addition and, without the addition of more alkali shall remain at 12 or higher for two hours and then at 11.5 or higher for an additional 22 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of pH measurement timing, the no-additional-alkali condition, and whether the two-hour and twenty-two-hour windows are met would change applicable numeric thresholds and whether missing time-series pH data reflects non-required monitoring or unresolved required evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 7 - The percent solids of sewage sludge that does not contain unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 75% based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge qualifies as lacking unstabilized primary solids, and how percent solids is calculated prior to mixing, would change whether the 75% threshold applies and how reported solids measurements are compared.

candidates.exact_span: Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or an anaerobic treatment process at the time the sewage sludge is disposed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretations of what treatment counts and the timing at disposal would change eligibility for Alternative 7, thereby changing the applicable numeric limit, monitoring requirements, and whether absent solids evidence is unresolved or reflects a different compliance pathway.
